item.description:
As you’ve passed by Calvary Baptist, have you wondered about the Memorial Stained Glass Window? Made up of fragments of stained glass retrieved from church windows during World War II, each Remembrance Service we describe the provenance of one fragment. item.title: Tracing the History of the Upper Beach — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — Centre 55
item.description:
Beaches Realtor Mark Battenberg invites you to an evening of discovery as he traces the wonderful history of the Upper Beach. From the decline of the great glaciers to the First Nations People, The Kingston Road during the war of 1812, and on to the villages of Norway an Benlamond, which were the cornerstones of the upper Beach, as it grew along The Kings Highway in the mid 1800’s. Discover Coleman’s Corners in Little York, the founding of East Toronto Village, and the rise and fall of the mighty Grand Trunk Railroad. Info: markbattenberg@rogers.com, 647-858-9708
Source: Beach Metro Community News

item.title: BOOK LAUNCH: STOP ANTIBLACK RACISM, by Nadia L. Hohn — Sat Nov 14, 2:00 PM — Blackhurst Cultural Centre
item.description:
📚🚀✊🏿Join award-winning author and educator Nadia L. Hohn for the launch of her latest release, STOP ANTIBLACK RACISM: 8 WAYS TO ACT NOW. In this practical book, part of the Take Action Series by Orca Book Publishers, Hohn identifies 8 steps for everyone - Black and non-Black people - to combat anti-Black racism. Together the steps offer readers practical ways to overcome ignorance, take a stand, and get back up after experiencing racism. The book includes a glossary and a list of resources for further exploration of the topic. Nadia is one of Toronto's favourite authors, bringing tremendous experience in education and publishing to her work - this is her 12th book! She not only writes but sings, plays the piano, draws - a true artivist! Come celebrate Nadia, her creativity, and her newest achievement, STOP ANTIBLACK RACISM, a book that teaches us all to take action! #ReadDifferently #socialjustice #CanLit #AfricanCanadian📚
Source: A Different Booklist

Try New Things in Toronto! ## 🍁 **Fall Walk: Glen Stewart Ravine & Beach Boardwalk Adventure!** 🍦🌊
Join us for a **beautiful fall walk** through one of Toronto’s most scenic spots — the **Glen Stewart Ravine** — followed by a stroll along the **Beach Boardwalk**!
We’ll take in the crisp autumn air, the colourful leaves, and the sound of the waves — plus a treat (or two) along the way.
Our walk begins at **Main Subway Station**, where we’ll make our way down **Main Street**, head east along **Kingston Road**, and then wander through the **Glen Stewart Ravine** — one of Toronto’s best hidden gems. item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Dancing Flowers — Mon Nov 2, 12:00 AM — Yorkville
item.description: Throughout the month of November the works of artist Mary Garrone are on display at the Yorkville Branch in an exhibit titled Dancing Flowers. Artist biography: A Toronto-based artist from Australia. She has studied abstract expressionism for two years with the techniques of Nicholas Wilton and Jenny Nelson. A flower photographer for many years, she continues with this subject matter in her acrylic and oil painting. Artist statement: I love the challenge of translating emotion into paintings using gesture, palette, value, shape and line. While each painting is an exhausting number of decisions for me, the artist, the goal is ultimately to bring joy to the viewer. Applying the visual principle that "lines activate," this series is entitled "There's a party in the garden and the flowers are dancing," with each piece conveying an unavoidably positive sensibility with gestures that deliver that message.
